subject.title: Model fallback selection ignores candidate context windows, causing overflow/compaction storms on mid-turn failover

question: When a known fallback candidate cannot fit the current assembled prompt, should OpenClaw skip it, compact to preserve configured order, or use a bounded hybrid policy?
rationale: Skipping changes explicit fallback ordering, while compaction persistently changes session state; source inspection cannot determine the intended compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Bounded hybrid preflight
options.body: Skip definitively undersized candidates when a later candidate fits, otherwise compact once for the best eligible configured candidate and fail clearly if it still cannot fit.

options.title: Preserve order by compacting
options.body: Always attempt to compact for each configured candidate, preserving operator order but accepting latency and persistent context-loss risk.

options.title: Skip undersized candidates only
options.body: Never compact during failover selection and advance past candidates that cannot fit, favoring session preservation over strict fallback order.

recommendation.title: Bounded hybrid preflight
recommendation.body: Skip definitively undersized candidates when a later candidate fits, otherwise compact once for the best eligible configured candidate and fail clearly if it still cannot fit.
